title: Assess Dify for a bounded self-hosted LLM platform pilot

context.description: Assess whether a small engineering team should run a bounded local Dify pilot for visual LLM workflows and retrieval applications. Current evidence is limited to public source files at one pinned revision; no Dify code or containers were executed.

constraints.description: Use only public evidence pinned to langgenius/dify revision ad90cb911138f6b27af996c87afe34fbb5a4ed16.
Do not infer runtime, performance, security, production fitness, or license compatibility from source documentation.
Require qualified human review of the modified license for the intended tenancy, branding, and distribution model.
Require a separately authorized sandboxed local pilot before adoption or deployment.
Require independent security and operations reviews before production use.

evidence.title: Pinned Dify main revision observation
limitations: The main branch can move after this observation; all file evidence is pinned to the observed commit.
The timestamp is normalized to the observation date; the exact retrieval second was not retained.

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata observation
limitations: Public visibility does not determine license compatibility.
The embedded observation is reproducible, but live repository metadata can change after the observation time.

evidence.title: Dify README at pinned revision
limitations: Feature and resource statements are upstream documentation claims, not runtime proof.

evidence.title: Dify modified license at pinned revision
limitations: This records technical evidence and is not legal advice.
A qualified human must assess the intended tenancy, branding, and distribution model.

evidence.title: Dify security policy at pinned revision
limitations: A disclosure policy does not establish that a release is secure or suitable for production.

evidence.title: Dify Docker Compose manifest at pinned revision
limitations: The manifest was inspected as text and not applied.
Services present in the manifest may be optional and do not prove default runtime behavior.

evidence.title: Dify Docker deployment guide at pinned revision
limitations: Documented deployment procedures were not executed.

claims.statement: Pinned upstream documentation describes workflows, retrieval, agents, model management, observability, APIs, and a self-hosting path relevant to this evaluation.
limitations: This establishes documented candidate relevance, not feature completeness or target-environment fitness.

claims.statement: Run only a bounded sandboxed local pilot after license review; do not adopt or deploy yet.
limitations: The recommendation does not authorize execution and does not establish production suitability.

hypotheses.statement: Dify is relevant enough to evaluate for visual workflows, retrieval applications, model integrations, and API access.
Dify can start and operate within the target local environment and resource budget.
The Dify license is compatible with the intended tenancy, branding, and distribution model.
The team can securely operate, observe, back up, upgrade, and recover the required Dify services.

checks.description: Confirm that inspected upstream files resolve from the recorded immutable commit and match recorded SHA-256 digests.
Obtain qualified review of the modified license for the exact intended use.
Run a separately authorized sandboxed local pilot and record startup, resource, integration, and teardown evidence.
Validate required services, secret handling, observability, backup, restore, upgrade, and rollback.
Perform a separate threat-informed security assessment of the selected release and configuration.

decision.summary: conditional-pilot: Dify is relevant enough for a bounded local evaluation, but adoption and deployment remain blocked.
decision.rationale: Pinned documentation supports candidate relevance and a documented self-hosting path. It does not provide runtime, operational, security, or license-fit proof.
limitations: No Dify application code, container, migration, plugin, or network-facing service was run.
License analysis is technical support, not legal advice.

actions.description: Complete qualified license review before deciding whether the intended use is permitted.
If license review permits evaluation, run the isolated local pilot and capture runtime evidence.
Complete independent security and operations reviews before any production decision.
